# Psalm 9 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the music director. A psalm of David. To the tune of 'Death of the Son.'

**2** I will praise You, LORD, with everything I have. I will tell about all Your amazing deeds.

**3** I will be filled with joy because of You. I will sing praise to Your name, Most High God.

**4** My enemies retreated; they stumbled and died in Your presence.

**5** You have upheld my right and my cause, sitting on Your throne and judging fairly.

**6** You have rebuked the nations and destroyed the wicked, erasing their names forever.

**7** The enemy is finished — an endless ruin! You have wiped out their cities — even the memory of them is gone.

**8** But the LORD reigns forever, ruling from His throne with perfect justice.

**9** He will judge the world with righteousness and govern the nations with fairness.

**10** The LORD is a shelter for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.

**11** Those who know Your name trust in You, for You, LORD, have never abandoned anyone who looks for You.

**12** Sing praises to the LORD, who rules from Zion! Tell the nations what He has done!

**13** For the God who avenges murder cares about the helpless. He does not ignore the cry of the suffering.

**14** LORD, have mercy on me. See how my enemies torment me. Snatch me back from the jaws of death,

**15** so I can praise You publicly at the gates of Jerusalem and rejoice in Your rescue.

**16** The nations have fallen into the pit they dug for others. Their own feet are caught in the net they set.

**17** The LORD is known by the justice He brings; the wicked are trapped by their own actions. Quiet meditation. Selah.

**18** The wicked will go down to the grave — every nation that ignores God.

**19** But the needy will not be forgotten forever; the hopes of the poor will not always be crushed.

**20** Arise, LORD! Don't let mere mortals triumph! Let the nations be judged in Your presence.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **9:16-17**: Poetic justice is a recurring theme in the Psalms: the wicked fall into their own traps. Justice is not imposed from outside — it grows from the nature of evil itself.

- **9:18-19**: The psalm refuses to let poverty be permanent. God's justice includes economic reversal — the forgotten will be remembered.

— PNEUMA
